This happened when I was 16 years old. I'm with my friend, it's getting late and we're bored out of our minds. We decide to go into town and ask someone to buy us beer. So, we get the alcohol and we head to the train tracks in our town. The tracks are abandoned and the whole train line around the town was a bit of a hotspot for underage drinking, particularly a dilapidated old train station, where a lot of people our age would meet and chill out. To get there you have to walk the line for about half a mile through hedges and small trees.

As we were too young for pubs and nightclubs, the tracks was considered the place to be. On a Saturday night it would be swarming with teens. This was Summer though, and a Wednesday night. The place was deserted, I had never walked the line and not seen at least a few groups we'd sort of know. We approach the old train station and are relieved to hear the sound of people, who appear to be singing.

We get closer and the singing begins to sound like chanting, it was really strange. I walk up to the building and peer through the window expecting to see people in the 15-18 age range. Instead, there's about 8 people all wearing black hooded robes, standing in a circle, chanting some weird sort of hymn. I'm ready to quietly get the fuck out of there when my friend, assuming they were people our age, shouts out "Well, what up faggots!!". I just run, and when he sees who's there he runs too. I didn't look back until we were off the track, but my friend said that he glanced back as he was running away and that there was at least 20 people around the train station, all wearing the same black hooded robes.

Really fucking strange, and to be honest, I'm not sure if that's even the creepiest thing that happened on that track. The place was just a magnet for weird shit.

It is incredible for the first 4-5 books, but then very unfortunately it declines and starts limping along slower and slower and slower. I stopped gave up on it after book 7 or 8. I was too frustrated with having read yet another one in which not much really happens to move the story forward. But like I said the first four or five books are brilliant.

I read the series when the last book came out. I think it was a great series and that it's even better now that you aren't waiting as the slow books were released. I just powered through the slower paced parts and I didn't really notice the complaints some of the others have noted with those books.
Was "powering through" the slower parts really a good strategy. Do you feel like you held the same bond with the characters as others have claimed?

The big powering through I did was having the ability to read through the next book immediately after the previous slow books. Those that read the series had a period of seven years where the books that were released were largely world building and stories that didn't progress the main plot. Many readers dropped off from reading the series during that time. For me I felt it was easier because I had the ability to just pick up the next book, as opposed to having to wait a couple years for the next book that didn't progress the overall plot. I guess you could say it was less powering through and more not having to dwell on the slower books for several years.

The first 3 books are tight (it was originally intended to be a trilogy.) Very Tolkien-esque. When my last gf read them she immediately said "This is a total Tolkien rip off," and in some ways it is quite formulaic. The magic system is interesting, and the characters are kind of annoying and sort of highschool level depth, but at the same time very interesting. Overall an interesting arc, some cool stuff happens, very epic level magic and happenings.

If you're into fantasy at all, you're kind of obligated to read it. There's no getting around it. Even if just so you can gripe with everyone else about how the middle of the series really sucked :)
